mainTopic: Immersing vessels at twilight and for a new purpose on יום טוב; which קרבנות may be brought on יום טוב and whether one may do סמיכה on them
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: the משנה can follow the רבנן if the whole משנה is about שבת. Next comes a ברייתא. The תנא קמא forbids immersing a טמא vessel at בין השמשות before יום טוב, and רבי שמעון שזורי forbids it even on a weekday because the vessel needs הערב שמש. The scholars of רב's study hall say the two argue about whether a man running to immerse at twilight shows he knows about הערב שמש. רבא disagrees and says the dispute is about an owner who doesn't know the lentil-size rule for a שרץ. A ברייתא then explains the משנה's words 'מגב לגב' and 'מחבורה לחבורה': an extra immersion for a new purpose is allowed on יום טוב. A new משנה brings the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about bringing שלמים and עולות on יום טוב and doing סמיכה on them. עולא limits the dispute to festival offerings and says everyone forbids נדרים ונדבות. A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר challenges him; the גמרא answers by fixing its wording, and רב יוסף answers instead that it is a dispute among תנאים, bringing another ברייתא as proof.

steps.title: A second explanation: the משנה follows the רבנן and is about שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to explain the earlier משנה. It follows the רבנן, and the entire משנה is talking about שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say the משנה follows the רבנן, and the whole משנה is speaking about שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the earlier discussion by giving a second, different answer about whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of matching the משנה to a different תנא, this answer says it fits the רבנן. Whatever the משנה forbids is forbidden because it is talking about שבת, not יום טוב. So the רבנן's more lenient view about יום טוב is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces an alternative answer

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: it follows the Rabbis,
and the entire mishna is speaking about Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the question from the previous section of the daf about whose view the משנה reflects.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-assigning the משנה's setting (שבת rather than יום טוב) so it fits the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to disagree with the רבנן, so it had to follow another תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה can follow the רבנן if every case in it is about שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא: no immersing at twilight before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a vessel that became טמא on ערב יום טוב may not be immersed during בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: a vessel that became impure on the day before יום טוב may not be immersed during twilight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about immersing a טמא vessel at twilight just before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בין השמשות is a time of doubt: it might still be the weekday, or it might already be יום טוב. Since immersing vessels on יום טוב is forbidden, the תנא קמא does not allow it during this doubtful time.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught: introduces a ברייתא
Twilight, a time when it is unclear if it is day or night

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּלִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: The Sages taught: a vessel that became impure on the eve of a Festival —
one may not immerse it during twilight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel that became טמא on ערב יום טוב may not be immersed at בין השמשות.

steps.title: רבי שמעון שזורי: not even on a weekday, because of sunset
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי says that even on a regular weekday you may not immerse the vessel at twilight, because it needs הערב שמש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי says: even on a weekday we don't immerse it then, because it needs the sun to set.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא gives a different and broader reason not to immerse at twilight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel that was immersed is fully טהור only after the sun sets. If you immerse it during the doubtful twilight time, it is unclear whether a sunset has already followed the immersion. So רבי שמעון שזורי's reason has nothing to do with יום טוב, which is why it applies on a weekday too.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion
Sunset, needed to finish the purification after immersion

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
Even on a weekday one may not immerse it,
phrases.notes: He means immersing it during twilight, the same time as in the first opinion.

phrases.english: because it requires sunset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersion at twilight is avoided even on a weekday because the vessel needs הערב שמש.

steps.title: Doesn't the first opinion also need sunset?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does the תנא קמא really not require הערב שמש?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא doesn't require sunset?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. It seems to make the תנא קמא hold that a vessel does not need sunset, which is hard to accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a vessel needs הערב שמש after immersion. So רבי שמעון שזורי's reason should be true for the תנא קמא too. Then what are they actually arguing about?

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real claim that the תנא קמא rejects הערב שמש. It is a question showing that the dispute cannot simply be about whether sunset is needed.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא לָא בָּעֵי הֶעֱרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ?
phrases.english: And does the first tanna not require sunset?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא לָא בָּעֵי הֶעֱרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the apparent difference between the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied position of the תנא קמא in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since רבי שמעון שזורי gives a reason that applies even on a weekday, the תנא קמא seems to disagree with it. But הערב שמש is a basic requirement that everyone accepts.

steps.title: רבא reports the view of רב's study hall: the dispute is whether intention shows from actions
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that the scholars of רב's study hall said the dispute is about מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו: whether a person's intention is evident from his actions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I found the Sages of רב's study hall sitting and saying that they disagree about whether a person's thinking can be seen from what he does.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reports an answer he heard from the scholars of רב's study hall. They say both sides agree sunset is needed, and the real argument is whether a person's actions reveal what he has in mind. רבא himself will reject this in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is no longer over the law of הערב שמש itself. It is over whether we can judge the situation by what the person's behavior shows he is thinking. The גמרא will now describe the exact case.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of רב's study hall
His intention is evident from his actions

steps.whyThisMatters: מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו is a general principle. Here it decides how we treat an act done during the doubtful twilight time.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רָבָא: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב
phrases.english: Rava said: I found the Sages of the school of Rav
sitting and saying,
about whether one's intention is evident from his actions
they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the dispute to a different underlying principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two תנאים seemed to argue over whether הערב שמש is required.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both require הערב שמש. They argue about מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו.

steps.title: What is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact situation in which this dispute plays out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what are the circumstances?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for a concrete case so the next line can describe it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The principle of intention showing from actions is abstract. The גמרא wants a real-life picture of where it changes the law of immersing at twilight.

phrases.english: And what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind רבא's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific scenario where the dispute about מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו applies

steps.title: A man running at twilight to immerse his vessel
steps.stepSummary: The case is a person holding a vessel and running during בין השמשות to immerse it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, someone is holding a vessel in his hand and running at twilight to immerse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the case: a person rushing during twilight with a vessel to immerse it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rushing is the 'action' that may reveal what he knows. He may be hurrying to immerse before dark because he knows the vessel needs הערב שמש before he can use it tonight. The question, answered in the next step, is whether his running really shows that he knows this.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding a vessel in his hand

steps.whatToRemember: According to the scholars of רב's study hall, both opinions in the ברייתא require הערב שמש. Their dispute is whether a person's rushing to immerse at twilight shows his intention clearly enough to matter. רבא will reject this reading in step 9.

phrases.english: for example, where one was holding a vessel in his hand,
and running along at twilight to immerse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is someone rushing at בין השמשות with a vessel in hand to immerse it.

steps.title: How each side reads the running man
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the man's running shows he knows the vessel needs הערב שמש. רבי שמעון שזורי says he may only be running because of his work.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage (the תנא קמא) holds: since this man is running to immerse his vessel, he clearly knows it needs הערב שמש. The other Sage (רבי שמעון שזורי) holds: he is running only because of his work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each side understands the man running at twilight to immerse his vessel. This finishes the first explanation of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the rushing proves the man knows sunset is needed, so he won't use the vessel too early, and a weekday immersion is fine. For רבי שמעון שזורי, the rushing proves nothing: he may just want to finish his work before dark. He might think the vessel is usable right away, so immersing at twilight is forbidden even on a weekday.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage holds (used for each side of a dispute)

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: הַאי דְּקָא רָהֵיט וְאָזֵיל —
phrases.english: One Sage holds: this one who is running along —
phrases.notes: This first 'Sage' is the תנא קמא, who allows immersing at twilight on a weekday.

phrases.english: he certainly knows that it needs sunset.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מֵחֲמַת מְלַאכְתּוֹ הוּא דְּקָרָהֵיט.
phrases.english: And the other Sage holds: it is because of his work that he is running.
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון שזורי. He means the man may just be hurrying to finish his work before dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: הַאי דְּקָא רָהֵיט וְאָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer in step 7 by applying the case of the running man to each side's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תנא קמא: the running shows he knows about הערב שמש. רבי שמעון שזורי: the running may come from his work, so it shows nothing.

steps.title: רבא's own explanation: a man who doesn't know the lentil-size rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees a person's intention can be seen from his actions. The dispute is about a vessel touched by less than a lentil-size of a שרץ, where the owner comes to ask the Rabbis whether it is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I (רבא) said to them: about the rule that a person's intention is seen from his actions, everyone agrees. They argue in a case like this: the vessel was touched by less than a lentil-size, and the owner came before the Rabbis to ask, 'Does it become impure from less than a lentil-size or not?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the first explanation and offers his own. He first sets up a new case, and the next step gives the two opinions on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first explanation, the dispute was about whether intention can be read from actions. רבא says both sides accept that rule, so the dispute must be somewhere else. He moves it to a man who shows he doesn't know a basic law of impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the size of a lentil

phrases.english: And I said to them:
phrases.notes: רבא is speaking. 'Them' are the scholars of רב's study hall from step 5.

phrases.english: Regarding 'his intention is evident from his actions' —
everyone agrees.
Where they argue is, for example,
where it became impure from less than a lentil-size,
phrases.notes: A dead שרץ only makes things impure if it is at least the size of a lentil. This owner doesn't seem to know that.

phrases.english: and he came before the Rabbis to ask:
Does it become impure from less than a lentil-size or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea that the dispute is about מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו and replaces it with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scholars of רב's study hall thought the sides argue over whether intention can be read from actions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides accept that rule. The dispute is about a man who shows he doesn't know the lentil-size rule.

steps.title: The two views on the man who asked
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי says that if he doesn't know this, he doesn't know about הערב שמש either. The רבנן say he only doesn't know this law, but he does know about הערב שמש.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds: since he hasn't learned this, he also hasn't learned about הערב שמש. The other Sage holds: this is what he hasn't learned, but הערב שמש he has learned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation by giving each side's view on the man who asked about the lentil-size rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון שזורי reasons that someone who is unsure of a basic purity law is probably unsure of הערב שמש too. He might use the vessel too early, so twilight immersion is forbidden even on a weekday. The רבנן say not knowing one detail doesn't mean he doesn't know the well-known need for sunset.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order. In step 8 the first 'מר' was the תנא קמא, but here the first 'מר' is רבי שמעון שזורי (the stricter one) and the second is the Rabbis.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of the dispute. (1) The scholars of רב's study hall: it depends on whether running to immerse shows he knows about הערב שמש. (2) רבא: everyone agrees intention can be read from actions; the question is whether not knowing the lentil rule means he doesn't know הערב שמש either.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: since he hasn't learned this,
phrases.notes: This time the first 'Sage' is רבי שמעון שזורי, who forbids immersing at twilight.

phrases.english: he also hasn't learned about sunset,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: הָא הוּא דְּלָא גְּמִיר,
phrases.english: And the other Sage holds: it is this that he hasn't learned,
but sunset he has learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's alternative by giving each side's reasoning on his case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each side's inference from the man's ignorance
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון שזורי: not knowing one law means he likely doesn't know הערב שמש. Rabbis: he still knows הערב שמש.

steps.title: What does 'from one back to another' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'מטבילין מגב לגב' and brings a ברייתא that asks what they mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may immerse from one back to another.' The Rabbis taught in a ברייתא: How does 'from one back to another' work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes a new phrase to explain it. This sets up the ברייתא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. The phrase 'מגב לגב' is unclear on its own, so a ברייתא is brought to define it.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'from one back to another': immersing again for a different purpose

phrases.english: And one may immerse from one back to another.
The Rabbis taught: How is 'from one back to another'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הערב שמש discussion and returns to explain a new phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the משנה means by immersing 'מגב לגב'.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: the winepress and the pitcher
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts its answer with someone who wants to immerse for his winepress on top of the immersion he did for his pitcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who wants to make (immerse for) his winepress on top of his pitcher...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins its explanation. This step only sets up the answer, and the next step finishes the sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a vessel already immersed for one use, his pitcher. Now the owner wants to immerse it again for another use, his winepress. That second immersion, 'on top of' the first, is what 'מגב לגב' means.

keyTerms.meaning: On top of / in addition to

phrases.english: One who wishes to make his winepress
phrases.notes: He means to immerse his vessel so it is pure enough for use in his winepress.

phrases.english: on top of his pitcher,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת גִּתּוֹ עַל גַּב כַּדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא's answer to the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A second immersion for the winepress on top of an earlier immersion for the pitcher; the next step completes the answer.

steps.title: The reverse case: pitcher on top of winepress
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes explaining 'מגב לגב': immersing a vessel again for the pitcher, on top of an immersion already done for the winepress, is also allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he wants to immerse for his pitcher on top of the immersion he did for his winepress, he may do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its answer from the last step by giving the reverse case. Here the first immersion was for the winepress, and the extra one is for the pitcher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both directions the vessel was already immersed once, and now the person wants a second immersion for a different use. This second immersion is extra and not really required. So it is allowed even on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: He may do it (it is permitted)

phrases.english: And his pitcher on top of his winepress — he may do it.
phrases.notes: This is the reverse of the last step. He already immersed for the winepress and now wants another immersion for the pitcher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's explanation of 'מגב לגב' begun in step 12 by adding the reverse case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An extra immersion for a different use, in either direction between winepress and pitcher, is permitted.

steps.title: Explaining 'from one group to another'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the second phrase of the משנה: someone who planned to eat with one group and now wants to eat with a different group may immerse again.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does 'from one group to another' work? He was going to eat with this group and now wants to eat with a different group. He has permission to immerse again.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks what 'מחבורה לחבורה' means and answers it right away. A person changes which eating group he joins and wants to immerse again for the new group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the pitcher and winepress case. He already immersed for the first group, so the second immersion is only extra. Because it is not really required, it is allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A group that eats a קרבן together, like the קרבן פסח
He has permission; he is allowed

steps.whatToRemember: Both 'מגב לגב' and 'מחבורה לחבורה' describe a second immersion that is not truly needed. That is why both are allowed on יום טוב.

phrases.english: How is 'from one group to another'?
He was going to eat with this group,
and now wants to eat with a different group —
he has permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing 'מגב לגב', the ברייתא moves on to explain the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Switching eating groups and immersing again for the new group is permitted.

steps.title: New משנה: peace offerings and burnt offerings on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow bringing שלמים on יום טוב, but without סמיכה, and do not allow עולות. בית הלל allow both, with סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: we bring peace offerings but do not lean our hands on them, and we do not bring burnt offerings. בית הלל say: we bring peace offerings and burnt offerings, and we lean our hands on them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a dispute about which קרבנות may be brought on יום טוב and whether one may do סמיכה on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate questions here. The first is which kinds of קרבנות may be brought at all: בית שמאי say only שלמים, while בית הלל say עולות too. The second is whether סמיכה, leaning hands on the animal, may be done on יום טוב: בית שמאי say no, and בית הלל say yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings; parts are eaten by people
Burnt offerings; burned completely on the מזבח
Doing סמיכה: pressing one's hands on the animal's head before it is slaughtered
The two great schools of תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two questions. For בית שמאי, bringing שלמים is allowed. Only the סמיכה on them is not allowed.

phrases.english: MISHNA: בית שמאי say:
One may bring peace offerings
but one does not lean hands on them,
but not burnt offerings.
And בית הלל say:
One may bring peace offerings and burnt offerings
and one leans hands on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים מְבִיאִין שְׁלָמִים וְאֵין סוֹמְכִין עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, separate from the immersion discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: שלמים may be brought without סמיכה, and עולות may not be brought. בית הלל: both may be brought, with סמיכה.

steps.title: עולא limits the dispute to the holiday's required offerings
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the dispute is about שלמי חגיגה, where the only question is סמיכה, and about עולת ראייה, where the question is whether it may be offered at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: the dispute is about the holiday peace offerings, whether to lean hands on them, and about the burnt offering of appearing, whether to offer it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with עולא defining exactly which קרבנות the משנה is arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא says the משנה is talking about the required holiday offerings, not just any שלמים or עולות. For שלמי חגיגה, both sides agree they may be brought, and they argue only about סמיכה. For עולת ראייה, they argue about whether it may be brought on יום טוב at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The peace offering every person must bring on the רגל
The burnt offering brought when 'appearing' in the בית המקדש on the רגל

steps.whyThisMatters: This is how the rest of the sugya will read the משנה: two required holiday offerings, with a different question about each one.

phrases.english: GEMARA: עולא said:
The dispute is about the holiday peace offerings, regarding leaning hands,
and about the burnt offering of appearing, regarding offering it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשַׁלְמֵי חֲגִיגָה לִסְמוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and narrows the dispute in the משנה of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute covers סמיכה on שלמי חגיגה, and whether עולת ראייה may be offered on יום טוב.

steps.title: The פסוק behind each side
steps.stepSummary: עולא shows the source for each view. בית שמאי read 'וחגותם' as allowing only the חגיגה. בית הלל read 'לה׳' as including anything brought to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold: 'You shall celebrate it as a festival to ה׳.' The חגיגה, yes; the עולת ראייה, no. בית הלל hold: 'To ה׳' means anything that is for ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא now gives the פסוק that each side reads differently. This explains their dispute about the עולת ראייה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same פסוק. בית שמאי focus on the word 'וחגותם', which sounds like חגיגה, so only the חגיגה is allowed on the day itself. בית הלל focus on the word 'לה׳', which includes every offering to ה׳, so the עולת ראייה is allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold; this is their view
'And you shall celebrate', a word that sounds like חגיגה

steps.whatToRemember: Same פסוק, different focus. בית שמאי read the word 'וחגותם', so only the חגיגה is allowed. בית הלל read the word 'לה׳', so everything for ה׳ is allowed, including the עולת ראייה.

phrases.english: For בית שמאי hold:
"You shall celebrate it as a festival to ה׳,"
the חגיגה offering — yes,
the burnt offering of appearing — no.
And בית הלל hold:
"To ה׳": anything that is for ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי וְחַגֹּתֶם אוֹתוֹ חַג לַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the dispute that עולא defined in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי learn from 'וחגותם' that only the חגיגה may be offered. בית הלל learn from 'לה׳' that every offering to ה׳ is allowed, including the עולת ראייה.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: vow and gift offerings are not brought on the festival
steps.stepSummary: עולא adds that even בית הלל agree that נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But vow-offerings and gift-offerings: all agree they are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא finishes his explanation by setting a limit: the dispute covers only festival offerings. Offerings the festival does not require, נדרים ונדבות, are forbidden according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל learned from 'לה׳' that more than the חגיגה may be brought, but only offerings that belong to the festival, like the עולת ראייה. A נדר or נדבה can be brought on any ordinary day, so there is no reason to bring it on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow-offerings: a person promises to bring an offering
Gift-offerings: a person sets aside a specific animal as an offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית הלל allow every kind of offering on יום טוב. Their wider view still covers only offerings that belong to the festival.

phrases.english: But vow-offerings and gift-offerings

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: all agree that they are not offered on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes עולא's statement by marking what lies outside the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to both בית שמאי and בית הלל, נדרים ונדבות may not be offered on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה says the same
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה states the same rule as עולא: נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too said רב אדא בר אהבה: vow-offerings and gift-offerings are not offered on a Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second אמורא who says the same rule, which backs up עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה states the rule without saying 'all agree,' but the word 'וכן' tells us he matches עולא. Two אמוראים now hold that non-festival offerings are not brought on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise said: brings someone who agrees
An אמורא who agrees with עולא here

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: And likewise Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Vow-offerings and gift-offerings
are not offered on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 18 with a second אמורא who holds the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's rule that נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רב אדא בר אהבה.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say בית הלל allow non-festival peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the dispute includes שלמים that are not of the festival, and בית הלל allow them. This contradicts עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, בית שמאי and בית הלל did not disagree about a non-festival עולה, which is not offered, or about festival שלמים, which are offered. They disagreed about the festival עולה and about non-festival שלמים: בית שמאי say he may not bring them, and בית הלל say he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא with a ברייתא. The ברייתא lists non-festival שלמים, which are נדרים ונדבות, as part of the dispute, and בית הלל permit them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said everyone agrees that נדרים ונדבות are forbidden. In this ברייתא, בית הלל allow non-festival שלמים, which are exactly נדרים ונדבות. So the ברייתא seems to directly contradict עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: They objected: brings a source that challenges a statement
A תנא who reports where the dispute really was
Belonging to the festival, meaning required because of it
He may not bring / he may bring

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the four cases straight. Agreed: non-festival עולה is forbidden and festival שלמים are allowed. Disputed: festival עולה and non-festival שלמים. The non-festival שלמים are what clash with עולא.

phrases.english: They objected:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל עוֹלָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: about a burnt-offering that is not of the Festival,
that it is not offered on the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל שְׁלָמִים שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and about peace-offerings that are of the Festival,
that they are offered on the Festival.
About what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל עוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: About a burnt-offering that is of the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל שְׁלָמִים שֶׁאֵינָן שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: and about peace-offerings that are not of the Festival.
For Beit Shammai say: He may not bring them,
and Beit Hillel say: He may bring them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיבִי, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule from steps 18 and 19 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that everyone agrees נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא places non-festival שלמים (נדרים ונדבות) inside the dispute and has בית הלל permit them, so not everyone forbids them.

steps.title: Fixing the ברייתא's wording to match עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the ברייתא: all non-festival offerings, both עולה and שלמים, are forbidden by everyone. The only dispute is the festival עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fix it and say this: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, בית שמאי and בית הלל did not disagree about non-festival עולה and שלמים, which are not offered, or about festival שלמים, which are offered. They disagreed only about the festival עולה: בית שמאי say he may not bring it, and בית הלל say he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by fixing the wording of the ברייתא. Non-festival שלמים move into the list of things everyone forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, non-festival שלמים were part of the dispute, which clashed with עולא. Now they join the non-festival עולה as agreed to be forbidden. The dispute shrinks to the festival עולה alone, which matches עולא exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Fix it and say this: the גמרא corrects a source's wording
That are not required by the festival

steps.whatToRemember: Picture after this rewording: offerings not required by the festival (נדרים ונדבות) are forbidden according to everyone. Festival שלמים are allowed according to everyone. The only dispute is the festival's עולה (עולת ראייה): בית שמאי forbid it and בית הלל allow it. רב יוסף gives a different answer in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not bringing a new ברייתא. It is correcting the wording of the same one so that it fits עולא.

phrases.english: Fix it and say this:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים שֶׁאֵינָן שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: about burnt-offerings and peace-offerings that are not of the Festival,
that they are not offered on the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל שְׁלָמִים שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and about peace-offerings that are of the Festival,
that they are offered on the Festival.
About what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל עוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: About a burnt-offering that is of the Festival,
for Beit Shammai say: He may not bring it,
and Beit Hillel say: He may bring it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 by fixing the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as first read put non-festival שלמים inside the dispute, with בית הלל allowing them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The corrected ברייתא puts all non-festival offerings among the things everyone forbids. Only the festival עולה is disputed, just as עולא said.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms עולא's view: on יום טוב, even בית הלל allow only offerings that belong to the festival.

steps.title: רב יוסף: This is simply a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects the need to reword the ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view is just one side of a dispute among תנאים, so it does not disprove עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Have you taken all the תנאים out of the world?! This is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different answer to the קשיא against עולא. He says the ברייתא does not have to be changed, because other תנאים disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 21 the גמרא changed the wording of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא so it would match עולא. רב יוסף keeps the ברייתא as it is. He says רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is one תנא, and עולא can follow a different תנא. The proof for that other תנא comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The sages of the משנה era (plural of תַּנָּא)
It is a dispute between תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not agreeing with the rewording of Step 21. He offers a separate answer: keep the ברייתא as written and treat it as a תנאים dispute.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Have you taken the Tannaim out of the world?!
phrases.notes: He means: why assume every תנא agrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר? Other תנאים can hold differently.

phrases.english: It is a dispute among Tannaim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the קשיא of Step 20 instead of the rewording given in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among Tannaim: the challenging source is one view, and עולא follows another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא seemed to disprove עולא unless its wording was changed.
steps.terutzMaskana: No change is needed. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is one תנא, and עולא follows a different תנא.

steps.title: A ברייתא where the dispute is only about festival peace-offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about שלמים brought because of יום טוב, and only about when to do סמיכה. This shows a תנא who frames the dispute differently from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Peace-offerings that come because of the festival, brought on the festival: בית שמאי say one does סמיכה on them on ערב יום טוב and slaughters them on יום טוב. בית הלל say one does סמיכה on them on יום טוב and slaughters them on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא to prove that another תנא disagrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. In this ברייתא, the argument is about the timing of סמיכה on festival שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא speaks only about שלמים that come because of the festival. It does not mention שלמים that are not connected to the festival, which fits עולא. The argument here is narrow: בית שמאי want the סמיכה done the day before, while בית הלל allow it on יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Leans his hands on the animal before it is slaughtered (סְמִיכָה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא gives עולא a תנא to stand on. Here the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל is only about festival שלמים, so it gives no support for bringing non-festival שלמים on יום טוב.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a Baraita:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלָמִים הַבָּאִים מֵחֲמַת יוֹם טוֹב בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: Peace-offerings that come because of the festival, offered on the festival,
Beit Shammai say:
One leans his hands on them on the eve of the festival,
and slaughters them on the festival.
And Beit Hillel say:
One leans his hands on them on the festival,
and slaughters them on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that backs up רב יוסף's claim that this is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that another תנא disagrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, which supports עולא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about סמיכה on שלמים brought because of the festival.
